stories.headline: United States and Canada pause 50 percent tariff threat after reaching trade deal
stories.body:
The United States and Canada have reached a temporary agreement to pause a major tariff threat against Canadian imports. US President Donald Trump announced late on Tuesday on Truth Social that he paused proposed 50% tariffs against Canada for a three-day period. The new 50% US tariffs threatened by the administration would have covered approximately $20 billion worth of Canadian goods.

Following the announcement, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer held a 45-minute meeting with his Canadian counterpart on Wednesday. Greer expressed optimism about the outcome of the discussions. He stated that officials feel confident they reached an agreement that will protect American workers, jobs, and supply chains while strengthening the North American economy. On Wednesday afternoon, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met with his cabinet and Canadian provincial leaders to brief them on the trade deal.

The pause comes after months of trade friction between the two neighboring nations. In February 2025, the White House hit Canada with a 25% tariff. US officials cited inadequate progress by Canada in curbing cross-border illegal immigration and drug trafficking as the reason for those tariffs. Trade between Canada and the United States is extensive, reaching an estimated $909 billion in 2024 according to the Office of the US Trade Representative. Canada is heavily reliant on this economic relationship, as nearly 72% of Canada's goods exports went to the United States last year.

Canadian public opinion has shown strong support for standing firm against American economic pressure. A poll by the firm Leger found that 56% of surveyed Canadians want Canada to take a hardline approach in trade negotiations with the United States. Canadian authorities have previously taken direct action against US trade measures. Last year, most Canadian provinces imposed a ban on US alcohol sales in retaliation to US tariffs. Cross-border energy projects have also seen past cancellations. Owner TC Energy halted the 1,200-mile Keystone XL pipeline project in 2021 after US President Joe Biden revoked a key permit.

stories.headline: Israeli military opens criminal probe after admitting forces shot at car carrying Hind Rajab
stories.body:
The Israeli military admitted on Wednesday that its troops opened fire in 2024 on a car carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab and six of her family members in Gaza. Hind Rajab died in January 2024 after making an emergency phone call to the Palestinian Red Crescent while trapped inside the vehicle. Palestine Red Crescent operator Rana Faqih stayed on the line for hours with the child while appealing to the Israeli army to allow an ambulance to reach her.

A 2024 Al Jazeera investigation indicated an Israeli tank was likely 13 to 23 metres away from the vehicle. Research agency Forensic Architecture and Earshot mapped 335 bullet holes on the body of the car. Her story drew international attention, and the docudrama 'The Voice of Hind Rajab', directed by Kaouther Ben Hania, premiered at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival on September 3, 2025.

The Israel Defense Forces stated that it has been conducting intensive combat across numerous fronts in an exceptionally complex operational reality for more than a thousand days. In a separate decision, the IDF ordered a military police criminal investigation into the March 2025 killing of 15 Palestinian medics and humanitarian personnel near Rafah. However, the military decided not to open a criminal investigation into April 2024 airstrikes that killed seven World Central Kitchen aid workers. In June, a UN commission reported that Israeli forces have killed more than 20,000 children and injured 44,000 in Gaza since October 2023.

stories.headline: Helicopter crash in Kenya kills seven people including five American citizens
stories.body:
A Eurocopter EC130 B4 helicopter crashed in Samburu county, Kenya, at approximately 09:13 local time on Wednesday, killing all seven people on board. The crash occurred near Mount Ololokwe. Emergency teams from the Kenya Red Cross participated in a multiagency response effort at the site. Tropic Air Kenya dispatched two of its helicopters to assist in search and rescue operations. By Wednesday evening, three bodies remained trapped in the wreckage due to ongoing flames.

A US State Department spokesperson confirmed that five of the seven people killed in the crash were US citizens. Among the victims was 55-year-old Jose Suarez, the president and general manager of several Telemundo stations in Florida. Ecuador's Strategic Intelligence Center Director General Michele Sensi-Contugi and his wife Stephany Hollihan were also killed in the incident.

Helicopter crashes have previously claimed high-profile lives in the region. In April 2024, Kenyan military chief Gen Francis Omondi Ogolla died in an army helicopter crash in western Kenya.

stories.headline: Former Ukrainian defence minister calls for elections as official is dismissed in corruption probe
stories.body:
Former Ukrainian defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov posted a video on YouTube on Tuesday calling for wartime presidential elections in Ukraine. Fedorov was fired as defence minister in mid-July, just six months after his appointment. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed Yevhenii Khmara as the new defence minister following Fedorov's dismissal. Elections have been suspended in Ukraine under martial law, which has been in effect since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Fedorov's call comes during ongoing government anti-corruption investigations. On Wednesday, Ukraine's deputy head of the presidential office Iryna Mudra was dismissed amid anti-corruption searches. Ukraine's anti-corruption agency NABU reported investigating a conspiracy involving the laundering of 150 million hryvnias through a state-owned bank to post bail for former energy minister Herman Haluschenko. In late 2025, former presidential chief aide Andriy Yermak resigned following a search of his home, and he was arrested in May on suspicion of money laundering.

Meanwhile, violent fighting continues in the country. On Wednesday, a Russian drone strike hit a minibus in the southern city of Kherson, killing four people.

stories.headline: Pakistan summons US diplomat after ambassador calls Jammu and Kashmir an important part of India
stories.body:
Pakistan's Foreign Ministry summoned the US Charge d'Affaires in Islamabad on Wednesday to lodge a formal demarche. The diplomatic protest came after US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor made statements during a visit to Srinagar. While visiting the region, Ambassador Gor stated, "This is an important part of India and so I'm here visiting for the first time".

During his visit to Srinagar, Ambassador Gor met with Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah at the chief minister's official residence. The diplomatic visit and remarks drew quick reaction from Pakistani officials and local political leaders in the region. Former Pakistan ambassador to the US Masood Khan criticized Gor's statements. Khan claimed that the remarks reflected a lack of understanding regarding the history of Jammu and Kashmir.

Local leaders also raised issues regarding travel policies during the visit. PDP president Mehbooba Mufti called on Ambassador Gor on the social media platform X to review and withdraw the existing travel advisory for Kashmir. The United States currently maintains a Level 4 "do not travel" advisory for Jammu and Kashmir.

stories.headline: Fire at Kolkata hotel building leaves nine people dead including four Bangladeshi citizens
stories.body:
A major fire broke out at around 1:45 am on Wednesday in a five-storey building housing several hotels on Mirza Ghalib Street in Kolkata, killing nine people. West Bengal Fire and Emergency Services Minister Kaushik Chowdhury stated that firefighters saved around 80 lives during the blaze. Kolkata Police reported that 60 people were rescued from the hotel building.

Four of the Bangladeshi nationals who died in the fire were identified as journalist Debashish Dutta, his wife Afsana Shimmin, their three-year-old son Sharnashish Dutta, and Md Akram Ali.

The tragedy in Kolkata comes just days after another fatal hotel fire in the state. Two days prior to the Kolkata fire, a hotel fire in Tarapith, located in the Birbhum district, also killed nine people.

stories.headline: India and Palestine sign agreements to build hospital and vocational center in West Bank
stories.body:
Indian Ministry of External Affairs Secretary Sripriya Ranganathan visited Ramallah on Wednesday and met with Palestinian Prime Minister Mohammad Mustafa. During the visit, Indian and Palestinian officials signed two memoranda of understanding. The agreements cover the construction of a 200-bed hospital in Jenin and a Technical and Vocational Education and Training Centre.

Following the agreements, Indian and Palestinian officials held a groundbreaking ceremony for the 200-bed super-speciality hospital in Arrabeh city, located in the Jenin Governorate. As part of the diplomatic mission, Sripriya Ranganathan handed over a consignment of life-saving medicines, including anti-cancer drugs, to the Palestinian health ministry.

In New Delhi, Palestinian Ambassador to India Abdullah M. Abu Shawesh held a press conference at the Palestinian embassy on Wednesday to discuss the developments.

stories.headline: Court sends former Delhi minister Satyendar Jain to 14-day judicial custody in corruption case
stories.body:
The Rouse Avenue Court remanded former Delhi minister Satyendar Jain and four other accused individuals to 14 days of judicial custody on Wednesday. The court order was issued in connection with an ongoing corruption investigation involving the Delhi Jal Board. In the same court proceeding, accused DJB employee Ankit Shrivastava was remanded to two days of Anti-Corruption Branch custody.

The arrests occurred a day prior to the court ruling. On Tuesday, the Anti-Corruption Branch arrested former Delhi Jal Board Chief Executive Officer Udit Prakash Rai along with Satyendar Jain and four others. The Anti-Corruption Branch alleged that Udit Prakash Rai and his family received Rs 1.52 crore in bribes linked to sewage treatment plant tenders.

The legal actions triggered political responses in the capital. AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal alleged that Union Home Minister Amit Shah directly ordered the arrest of Satyendar Jain.
